title: AI music & sound
content_html:
What You'll Do

In this project you'll make original music with AI — beats and short soundtracks created from a simple text description. You'll score imaginary scenes (a movie trailer, a game level, a walk through Nairobi) and make beats you could picture in a song. Along the way you'll discover how AI "listens" to patterns in existing music to build something new, and you'll think about creativity, originality, and who owns a song a machine helped make.

By the end you'll have made at least one original AI track, given it a title and a purpose (like "battle music for a video game"), and worked out how the AI understood your instructions.

What You'll Need

  • An AI music tool. Pick one: Soundraw (soundraw.io, instrumental beats by mood and genre), Boomy (boomy.com, beginner-friendly songs), AIVA (aiva.ai, orchestral/soundtrack style), or Suno (suno.com, full songs with vocals). Most need a free account and give you a limited number of tracks per day.
  • Headphones or a speaker to listen.
  • Good to know: these tools need internet and each track takes 30 seconds to a couple of minutes to make. Use the wait to plan your next version.

Steps

  1. Think for a minute: where have you heard music or sound made by a computer? (Game music, ringtones, adverts.) Today you'll make your own.
  2. Open your tool and make one quick track to see how it works — try the style "upbeat, hopeful, hip-hop, 30 seconds." Play it.
  3. Here's the idea: the AI has learned patterns from thousands of songs — rhythms, chords and instruments that usually go together. When you give it a mood or genre, it recombines those patterns into something new.
  4. Pick a theme for your soundtrack — "music for exploring a jungle," "beats for a superhero," "calm music for studying."
  5. In your tool, choose a mood/genre that matches your theme and generate a track.
  6. Make at least 2 versions, changing just one thing each time (tempo, mood, or instrument). Notice how your change affects the result.
  7. Name your final track and write one sentence saying where it'd be used — e.g. "Fast Feet — background music for a running game."
  8. Using Suno? Try adding lyrics: "Write an upbeat Afrobeat song about friendship in Nairobi."
  9. Play your favourite track (about 30 seconds) for a friend or the group, then say what surprised you about what the AI made.

Examples to Try

  • "Jungle Steps" — a 45-second instrumental from the prompt "adventurous, tribal drums, jungle theme," made to score an explorer game level.
  • "Nairobi Nights" — an Afrobeat/pop instrumental at a medium tempo: "music for a matatu ride through the city at night."
  • "Friendship Anthem" — a full song with AI vocals from the prompt "Afrobeat song about friendship, happy mood," chorus and all.

Tips

  • Change one thing at a time. If you change the mood and the tempo and the genre at once, you won't know which change did what.
  • Weird or repetitive result? That's a real limit of AI music — treat it as something to notice, not a mistake to fix.
  • Downloads: some free tools let you make and preview tracks but lock the high-quality download behind a paid plan — a screen recording or screenshot of your track still counts.
  • No headphones? Take turns listening to one track at a time on a speaker.

Think About It

  • How do you think the AI "knows" what a happy or a sad song sounds like?
  • Is an AI making music the same as a human composer writing it — or different?
  • If an AI makes a song, who owns it — you, the AI, or the company that built the tool?
  • Did the AI make exactly what you imagined, or something different? Why?
  • Should AI-made music be allowed in films, adverts, or on the radio? Why or why not?

Challenge Yourself

  • Easy: Make two versions of the same theme changing only the mood ("happy" vs "mysterious") and compare how different they sound.
  • Medium: Build a 3-track "mini soundtrack" for a short scene — calm intro, tense middle, triumphant ending — and explain your prompt choices.
  • Hard: Record your own voice or a clap rhythm on a phone, mix it with an AI beat to make a short "remix," and explain how you blended the human and AI parts.
